name: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Type 29
aliases: Combined Mitochondrial Oxidative Phosphorylation Deficiency Type 29

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Early onset multisystemic clinical features including neurological and muscular symptoms
Demonstration of combined defects in multiple respiratory chain enzyme complexes in muscle or fibroblasts
Identification of pathogenic variants in nuclear genes affecting oxidative phosphorylation
Brain MRI showing basal ganglia and brainstem abnormalities consistent with mitochondrial dysfunction
Elevated blood or CSF lactate levels indicating mitochondrial respiratory chain dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of early onset multisystemic clinical features plus biochemical evidence of combined respiratory chain defects and genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data due to phenotypic heterogeneity.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I
Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex III

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate levels
Combined deficiency of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes I, III, and IV enzyme activities in muscle biopsy
Elevated serum creatine kinase in some cases
imaging: Brain MRI showing bilateral basal ganglia and brainstem signal abnormalities
Cerebral and cerebellar atrophy in advanced stages
genetic: Pathogenic variants in nuclear genes encoding mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation components or assembly factors
other: Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and abnormal mitochondrial morphology on electron microscopy

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated complex I deficiency rather than combined defects
Characteristic symmetrical necrotizing lesions in basal ganglia and brainstem
Often caused by single complex deficiencies or mtDNA mutations

redFlags: Severe lactic acidosis refractory to treatment
Multisystem involvement including cardiomyopathy and liver dysfunction
references: Rahman S, et al. Mitochondrial disease: clinical features and diagnosis. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2020.
Parikh S, et al. Diagnosis and management of mitochondrial disease: a consensus statement from the Mitochondrial Medicine Society. Genet Med. 2015.
